title: Exploring Atlanta’s Midtown Neighborhoods with May Mobility and Lyft

body_markdown:
How riders can experience May Mobility’s autonomous vehicle technology through Lyft while getting around Atlanta


Getting around Atlanta can mean everything from meeting friends for lunch in Old Fourth Ward to spending an afternoon along the BeltLine or catching a show in Midtown. For eligible Lyft riders, some of those everyday trips come with the chance to ride in a May Mobility autonomous vehicle (AV).


In 2025, we[launched](https://maymobility.com/en/get-a-may/atlanta) our first public AV deployment with Lyft, making our AVs available to eligible riders through the Lyft app. The partnership combines our autonomous driving technology with Lyft’s rideshare network, giving Atlantans a way to experience autonomous transportation through a platform they already know and use.


**How to hail a May Mobility AV in Atlanta**


For riders, the experience starts just like a typical Lyft trip. Within our available service area around Midtown, Virginia-Highland and Old Fourth Ward, riders can request a standard or Wait & Save ride and, depending on availability, may be matched with one of our AVs. Each ride includes a trained standby operator in the driver’s seat, who monitors the trip and can take over if needed.


## Hail May Mobility on Lyft


Request a standard or Wait & Save ride


The experience may feel familiar, but there’s a lot happening behind each ride. Our[fifth-generation autonomous driving system](https://maymobility.com/en/news/may-mobility-launches-new-av-architecture) combines deep learning, a predictive world model and intelligent real-time reasoning to help our vehicles understand and respond to complex real-world environments.


The architecture is designed to help our AVs adapt to new geographies and situations without the intensive data and compute requirements that can limit typical autonomy systems. Atlanta puts those capabilities to work in a dynamic urban environment, navigating the traffic, streets and everyday situations that come with moving people through different neighborhoods.

**A day with May in Midtown Atlanta**


Our technology comes to life through the trips people take every day.


Old Fourth Ward, for example, offers an easy starting point for an afternoon out. Riders can grab a bite to eat at[Ponce City Market](https://poncecitymarket.com/) before heading to the[Atlanta BeltLine’s Eastside Trail](https://beltline.org/) , which connects parks, restaurants, shops and public art across several neighborhoods.


Using Lyft can also make a day like this more flexible. Instead of planning a walk around where the car is parked, riders can explore the BeltLine in one direction and request an eligible Lyft ride from elsewhere in the service area, during service hours, when they’re ready for their next stop.


## High Museum of Art


Woodruff Arts Center


From there, a trip into Midtown can put riders near some of Atlanta’s best-known arts and cultural destinations. They might visit the[High Museum of Art](https://high.org/) at the Woodruff Arts Center, explore the surrounding neighborhood or catch a performance at the historic[Fox Theatre](https://www.foxtheatre.org/) . These trips may look different for every rider, and that’s part of the point. Autonomous transportation is most useful when it can support the variety of ways people actually move through a city.

### Making autonomy feel like part of everyday life


Atlanta offers a glimpse of what autonomous transportation can look like when it’s integrated into an existing transportation network, rather than treated as a separate experience. Through our partnership with Lyft, riders can encounter our technology through a familiar platform and use it for the same kinds of trips they already make.


At the same time, Atlanta gives us an opportunity to demonstrate how our autonomous driving technology can operate in the complexity of a real city, from busy streets and changing traffic conditions to the everyday situations that come with moving people between neighborhoods.


Our vehicles run daily during limited hours around Midtown. Riders who’d prefer a human driver can decline an autonomous match in the Lyft app. To see where else we operate, visit[our Rides page.](https://maymobility.com/en/ride)
